# dsh-speak
Read text aloud in the DeepSeek Harness (DSH), on the machine running it, with the macOS `say` comma
d text aloud in the DeepSeek Harness (DSH), on the machine running it, with the macOS `say` command.
**English** | 中文
| Entry | Where | What it does |

| `speak` tool | the model can call it | reads text aloud, or stops with `stop: true` |
| 🔊 message
action | the action strip under every finalized assistant reply | click to read that reply, click ag

ain to **stop** |
| 🔊 select-to-read bubble | above any text you select on the page | "select and re

ad", like select-to-translate |
| ⚙ reading settings | speaker-gear button in the composer dock | pe
r-language voice, rate, and Han-character bias |
Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean are detected per character, and **every script run is read by
its own system voice** in its own `say` process. One reading plays at a time; a new request replace
own system voice** in its own `say` process. One reading plays at a time; a new request replaces it.
Audio comes out of the machine running DSH, never the browser. No network calls, no API keys, no mod
ut of the machine running DSH, never the browser. No network calls, no API keys, no model downloads.
## Requirements
- **macOS** — playback shells out to `say`. (Linux with `spd-say`, or a browser-side `speechSynthesi

s` variant, would be a separate provider; not implemented.)
- **DSH 0.2.x** — the desktop app, or an

y profile whose page is served to a browser.
- **Node 20+** only if you want to run the offline test

profile whose page is served to a browser.

## Install
### A. Through the plugin manager (recommended)

1. Open DSH → **Plugins** (Settings → Plugins, or the Plugins panel in the sidebar).
2. **Install bu
ndle** and paste the repository URL:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A git URL, a local absolute path, and an npm name are all accepted.
3. The bundle patch inserts one
row (`speak`) and the browser half is served automatically — there is no build step and no dependenc

ies to install.
4. Use it. If the buttons do not appear, reload the page once.
> The in-app plugin manager is the intended path for the desktop app, which is why the `dsh plugin`
CLI refuses that profile. For any other profile the CLI works too — see below.
### B. Manual install into a profile
Use this when you want the plugin to live outside the profile's `node_modules`.
1. Copy the package next to the profile's patch file:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. Add one row to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The `name` **must point at the entry file**: the loader resolves a `.`-prefixed name with `import(ne
w URL(name, baseUrl))`, so a directory cannot be imported, and the browser half is found by walking
up from that file to the nearest `package.json`.

3. Restart the app, or let the profile reload — an **added** row is picked up live.
4. To change hos
t code later: write a **new file** (`index.v2.js`…) and **remove then re-insert** the row. A mounted
row is not re-imported when only its `name` changes, and a `?v=` query in the name is rejected by t
he loader. `deploy.sh` automates exactly this.
### C. A `dsh web` profile

That installs the package; the bundle also has to be listed in that profile's `package.json` → `dsh.
profile.bundles` for its patch to be applied. The in-app plugin manager does both steps for you.
## Use
### Ask the assistant
> "read this aloud" / "读一下这段" / "stop reading" / "别读了"
| `speak` argument | Meaning |

| `text` | text to read; markdown is stripped; required unless `stop` is true |
| `stop` | `true` st

ops the current reading instead of starting one |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
Two halves in one package (one loader row):
- `index.js` — the host half. Registers the `speak` tool and four routes on the composition's web se
dex.js` — the host half. Registers the `speak` tool and four routes on the composition's web server:
| Route | Purpose |

| `POST /api/dsh-speak` | `{action:"speak", text?/sessionId+messageId}` or `{action:"stop"}` |
| `GE
T /api/dsh-speak/status` | what is playing now: source, message identity, languages, voices, sequenc

e, progress |
| `GET/POST /api/dsh-speak/settings` | read/write preferences; lists installed voices

|
| `GET/POST /api/dsh-speak/client` | the browser half's report channel (see *Diagnostics*) |
- `client.js` — the browser half, a prebuilt bundle in the format the client module loader expects (
`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`). It registers four slots: `conversation.chat.assistan
t-actions`, two entries in `shell.overlay`, and `conversation.composer.dock`.
Language handling:
- Kana makes a Han/kana run Japanese; Hangul is Korean; Latin is English; a kana-free Han run follow

s the **Bare Han** setting.
- Sentence-ending punctuation and script changes split runs, so `中文句子。日本

語の文。` keeps two voices.
- Latin runs shorter than `MIN_LATIN_RUN` (12 characters of their own script
, default) are folded into the surrounding language, so an acronym inside Chinese prose does not fli

p the voice for three words. CJK and Hangul runs are never absorbed.
- Playback is one `say` process
per run, started when the previous one exits: `say` has **no inline voice switch** (its `[[...]]` c
ommands cover rate, pitch, volume, and input mode only), and an unsupported `[[voice:…]]` is read ou
, pitch, volume, and input mode only), and an unsupported `[[voice:…]]` is read out as literal text.
## Security notes
- Routes only accept `POST`/`GET` and require `application/json`, so a cross-origin page hits a CORS
preflight it cannot pass, and a simple request is rejected with 415. Text never leaves the machine

— it goes straight to `say`.
- The plugin deliberately does not apply DSH's connection trust fence t
o its routes, so they can be exercised with `curl`. It only ever makes the host speak.
